x.name: alphaXiv
x.bio: High fidelity research

tweets.text:
“Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain”

World models may work better when reasoning and causality live in code instead of being learned entirely from pixels.

So this paper uses a coding agent as the brain of a world model, with code maintaining persistent state and rules while a video model renders the visuals.

Then there's a lightweight proxy connects them, letting code decide what happens and video generation decide how it looks.

https://t.co/WO6Ow4VfsR

“One Policy, Many Embodiments”

This Xiaomi paper suggests to unify manipulation geometry first, then specialize control only at execution time.

They introduced UCAG-P, a VLA trained across humans, single-arm robots, bimanual robots, and humanoids using one shared action representation.

So it predicts camera-centric 3D motion of the wrist and grasp center, then translates that geometry into each robot’s native actions.

This lets one policy learn directly from heterogeneous robot data and human videos without explicit retargeting.

https://t.co/4PtuZIZauU

“VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning”

This paper builds 300 procedural tasks for models to reason directly through images and video, with verifiable rewards for training and evaluation.

They find that visual trajectories matter more than textual Chain-of-Thought, with performance collapsing when intermediate images are removed but barely changing when reasoning text is replaced.

So for many spatial and dynamic tasks, models may reason better by thinking in visual states rather than language.

https://t.co/983XhODYgP

If you lead AI for an enterprise, the highest leverage thing you can do is to make your AI stack model agnostic. 

There are two things I would invest in.

This gives you the flexibility to switch models, customize them, compare them on your own workloads, and optimize for the best combination of quality, cost and latency.

x.name: Aaron Levie
x.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
This week’s tech earnings calls were a critical reminder of how valuable the relationship is between software and AI.

Software provides the guardrails for how data is managed, how business logic in workflows are maintained, how you manage and govern access to information, how you protect data, and more. You want these systems to work the same way every time, without fail. 

Agents, on the other hand, work inside these systems and with this data to execute on tasks just like people would have. But at a scale far greater than people ever did, which is especially why the deterministic controls matter more than ever.  

And in fact many of the best ways to deploy agents will be directly within the software systems themselves, like from Salesforce, Box, Harvey, ServiceNow, and so on. These platforms can optimize agents for their workflows and domains, with evals and context that are unique to their vertical, as well as connect to other 
 agents headlessly. 

The net result is both software and AI adoption go up, hand in hand. Software and Agents are going to work together, and ultimately grow the size of the IT TAM dramatically as a result over time.
